Cooling Questions Westchester Homeowners Ask Before Booking

tabs.tab_title: How do I know which air conditioning service to schedule?
tabs.tab_content: Schedule repair when the system has stopped cooling, produces unusual sounds, leaks, short cycles, or behaves differently. Choose maintenance when it is operating but due for preventive care. Installation is for spaces without an existing system; replacement swaps out current equipment. If unsure, describe the symptoms when booking.

tabs.tab_title: Should I repair or replace my air conditioner?
tabs.tab_content: Repair often makes sense when the system is relatively new, the problem is isolated, and it has otherwise been reliable. Replacement may be more practical when the AC is older, needs repeated service, uses more energy, or requires an expensive major component. A trustworthy recommendation explains both options.

tabs.tab_title: Is AC maintenance worthwhile if my system seems fine?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. Many electrical, drainage, airflow, and performance problems develop before obvious symptoms appear. Maintenance lets a technician check for deterioration while the system is still operating, reducing avoidable strain and catching concerns early.

tabs.tab_title: How much do professional cooling services cost?
tabs.tab_content: Pricing depends on the service, equipment type, required parts, accessibility, and whether emergency scheduling is needed. Before approving work, ask whether the estimate includes diagnosis, parts, labor, system testing, and warranty coverage — and whether after-hours service costs more.

tabs.tab_title: When does an AC problem require emergency service?
tabs.tab_content: Call promptly if the system repeatedly trips a breaker, produces a burning smell, leaks near electrical components, makes loud mechanical noises, or stops cooling during dangerous heat. Uneven cooling, rising bills, or weakening airflow are less urgent but should still be addressed.
